messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Memory
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Memory

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Kamal had always taken pride in his work as an environmental scientist. His dedication to preserving the natural world was evident in every project he undertook. But one fateful day, while working on a conservation site, Kamal's life took a devastating turn. In a moment of distraction, he accidentally triggered a machine that crushed a colleague's leg, leaving them with serious injuries. The event replayed in Kamal's mind like a horror movie. When he remembered the frightening scene, he felt as though it was happening all over again – the sound of his colleague's screams, the sight of their mangled leg, and the feeling of helplessness that washed over him (Reliving Event). It was as if time had frozen, and Kamal was trapped in that moment. The memory was so extreme that he struggled to believe it actually happened to him; it felt like a surreal nightmare (Story Feels Unreal). Kamal's wife, Leila, noticed the change in him immediately. He became withdrawn, avoiding social gatherings and events where he might encounter reminders of the accident. Heavy breathing sounds, like those he had heard his colleague make as they struggled for air, now sent Kamal into a panic (Triggers: Auditory - Breathing). Even something as innocent as Leila's affectionate hugs made him recoil; physical touch brought back the memory of the crushing machine and the weight of his responsibility (Triggers: Expressions of Affection). Feeling happy or relaxed was also a trigger, as it reminded Kamal of the carefree days before the accident. When he did experience moments of joy, they were short-lived, as the guilt and anxiety that followed inevitably dragged him back down (Triggers: Feeling Happy). These triggers seemed to be everywhere, constantly threatening to unleash the torrent of memories that Kamal struggled to keep at bay. When Kamal tried to talk about the accident, he found himself unable to find the words. The memory was so vivid, yet he couldn't seem to articulate it; it was as though his brain had become tangled in a knot (Memory: Cannot Find Words). Leila's attempts to console him only made things worse, as her concern and empathy brought back the feelings of responsibility that haunted him. As time went on, Kamal became increasingly isolated. His work suffered, and he struggled to connect with his loved ones. The weight of his memories and the constant barrage of triggers had taken a toll on his mental health. It was only when Leila threatened to leave him if he didn't seek help that Kamal realized he needed support. He began attending therapy sessions, hoping to find a way to break free from the cycle of guilt, anxiety, and avoidance that had consumed his life. Now, as Kamal sits in his therapist's office, he is most afraid of being unable to forgive himself for the accident. He hopes that, with time and support, he will be able to learn to live with his memories and find a way to heal.
